title: K2tog: right-leaning decrease
subtitle: Knitting two stitches together as one.
excerpt: K2tog (knit two together) is the simplest decrease in knitting. It inserts the needle through two stitches at once and knits them as one, reducing the stitch count by one and creating a right-leaning line in the fabric.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), decreases chapter. Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: Knit two together: a right-leaning single decrease worked by inserting the needle through two stitches simultaneously and knitting them as one. Reduces the stitch count by one.

content.text: K2tog (abbreviated from knit two together) is the most common decrease in knitting patterns. The needle enters two stitches at once rather than one, and the yarn is wrapped and drawn through both simultaneously. The resulting stitch leans to the right.

is paired with SSK (slip, slip, knit) in symmetric shaping, because SSK leans to the left. The two together frame every decrease motif in lace and every shaping line in a garment. Difficulty: beginner.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows worked
Work to the position where the decrease is needed.
Insert the right needle from left to right through the front of the first two stitches at once, as when knitting a single stitch.
Wrap the yarn and draw a single loop through both stitches.
Drop both stitches off the left needle. One new stitch on the right needle; stitch count reduced by one.

K2tog appears on virtually every decrease row in every lace pattern, where it is always paired with a yarn over to maintain stitch count. In hat crowns it is worked at regular intervals to reduce the stitch count for the final crown. Sock toe shaping uses k2tog on the right side of the toe and SSK on the left. In lace, k2tog leans right; the chart symbol is a triangle or line slanting right.

items.symptom: The stitch leans the wrong direction
items.cause: Worked SSK instead of k2tog, or the needle entered from the wrong direction
items.fix: Confirm the needle enters from the left (as for a knit stitch) through both stitches. If it entered from the right, you are working a variation that will lean differently.

items.symptom: The two stitches are tight and hard to enter together
items.cause: Knitting at a tight tension, or the two stitches are close to the needle tip
items.fix: Push both stitches slightly down the left needle so they are open before inserting the right needle. If tension is consistently very tight, try a needle one size larger.

items.symptom: Lace chart shows a hole but no hole appeared
items.cause: K2tog was worked but the paired yarn over was forgotten
items.fix: In lace, every k2tog (or SSK) should be accompanied by a nearby yarn over on the same row to maintain stitch count. Re-read the chart row.
